text:
ACTION: REFER_NOW
STM: NEWBORN BABIES - DRUG DOSES: FOR BABIES LESS THAN 4 WEEKS
---
Bebi no save dring gut: diswan hem saen blong denja. Kolem AHC o hospital long radio o fon nao.
Givim ampicillin 260 mg (50 mg fo evri kilo) IV o IM sapos yu garem, an gentamicin 26 mg (5 mg fo evri kilo) IV sapos yu garem.
Keepim bebi warm, putum IV line sapos yu save, an givim susu o wata long spoon sapos hem save tekem.
Talem long dokta: bebi 2 manis, 5.2 kg, no save dring gut, hot bodi, no transport.
Sapos bebi go moa sik, kolem bak kwiktaem.

ACTION: REFER_NEXT_TRANSPORT
STM: URINARY TRACE INFECTION
---
Bebi 2 monts garem hot bodi an no kaikai gud: hem sistemia sik, mas go long hospital.
Givim trimethoprim 20 mg (4 mg fo evri kilo) long maot evri 12 aoa taem yu wet.
Sapos no garem trimethoprim, givim co-trimoxazole 20 mg (4 mg fo evri kilo) evri 12 aoa.
Givim susu plande, an sapos hem no dring gud, putum IV o NGT wata.
Kolem dokta long AHC long radio nao, talem bebi 2 monts, 5.0 kilo, hot bodi, no kaikai gud, smel pispis.
Lukluk fo saen blong denja: toraot evri samting, slip tumas, no fit dring, sek-se

ACTION: ADVISE
STM: SKIN DISEASES
---
This looks like scabies with infection: red, painful, pus present.
Give cloxacillin 520 mg orally every 6 hours for 7 to 10 days (25 mg/kg, max 500 mg, so use the max dose).
Dilute benzyl benzoate 1:1 (25 ml with 25 ml water), wash and dry the child, then apply all over body below the neck, between fingers and toes.
Leave the lotion 24 hours, wash off, and repeat after 1 week.
Treat all household members and wash all bedding and clothes in hot water, dry in the sun.
Come back in 2 days if the sores are worse, the child has fever, or the eyes are involved.

ACTION: REFER_NOW
STM: COLDS/ URTI
---
Convulsion is a danger sign. Refer this baby to hospital now, do not wait.
The guideline I found is about simple colds without danger signs, so it does not cover this.
Do a malaria RDT if you can, and tell the hospital the result.
Keep the baby warm, on her side, and give oxygen if you have it.
Call the AHC or hospital by radio or phone now.
Write the referral note: age, weight, runny nose, cough, convulsion time, RDT result.

ACTION: REFER_NOW
STM: PERTUSSIS (WHOOPING COUGH)
---
Pikinini garem kof fit tumas an toroaot afta kof, an hem no fit dring gud. Diswan saen blong denja.
Kolem hospital o AHC long radio o phone nao, talem olketa fo tekem hem.
Long taem yu wet, letem hem sidaon op, no putum eni samting long maot blong hem.
Sapos hem no fit dring, no forcim.
Talem long dokta: kof 10 dei, toroaot afta kof, no fit dring, 18 manis, 9.9 kilo.

ACTION: ASK_PERSON
STM: NONE

Ask the nurse in charge or phone the doctor at the AHC for the correct treatment.
Check for danger signs: not able to drink, vomiting everything, fits, very sleepy, fast breathing, stiff neck.
If any of those are present, refer now and do not wait for the medicine.
Keep the skin clean and dry and wash the bedding and clothes in hot water.

Talem mama fo no letem pikinini stap long haos yet, an kolem NRH o AHC long fon o radio kwiktaem.
Askem nes in charge o dokta long klinik fo helpem wetem report.

ACTION: ADVISE
STM: EARLY ESSENTIAL NEWBORN CARE
---
Keep baby skin-to-skin with mother for the full 90 minutes if baby is well, or keep warm with hat and wrap if not.
Give vitamin K 1 mg IM once using the 1 mg/1 ml ampoule, never the 10 mg/ml.
Give hepatitis B and BCG vaccines now.
Apply tetracycline eye ointment to both eyes.
Weigh and examine: this baby is under 2.5 kg so follow the low birth weight guideline too.
If breathing is fast over 60 a minute or baby looks unwell, give oxygen by nasal catheter and treat for infection, then send.

ACTION: ASK_PERSON
STM: NONE
---
I am not sure. The guideline I found is about syphilis, not urinary infection.
Ask the nurse in charge or the doctor on the radio for the URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS section.
Check if the child can pass urine and if the abdomen is swollen.
If the child cannot pass urine, vomits everything, or becomes very sleepy, send now by any means.

ACTION: ADVISE
STM: MALARIA
---
Givim artemether-lumefantrine 1 tablet long moning an 1 tablet long naet fo 3 dei, wetem kaikai o susu.
Sapos no artemether, askem dokta long fon fo wanem meresin blong givim.
Kambak kwiktaem sapos hem no fit dring, toraot evri samting, sek-sek, slip tumas, o urine hem dark yellow o brown.
Kambak long 3 dei sapos hem stap gud.

ACTION: REFER_NOW
STM: OTITIS MEDIA - ACUTE & CHRONIC
---
Bebi garem saen blong denja: brit hariap tumas, no fit dring, pus long ia. Sendem hem go long hospitol long truk nao.
Givim amoxycillin 410 mg (50 mg fo evri kilo) long maot sapos hem save dring smol.
Sapos hem no save dring, no givim long maot, kolem AHC long radio fo helpem.
Kipim hem warm, letem hem sidaun long maot sapos hem save.
Kolem dokta long hospitol talem olketa hem kam.
Raetem referral leta: 9 months, 8.2 kg, pus long ia, brit hariap, no fit dring, taem blong meresin.

ACTION: ADVISE
STM: SKIN DISEASES
---
Yes, start treatment today. Give cloxacillin 150 mg by mouth every 6 hours for 7 to 10 days (25 mg/kg).
Apply benzyl benzoate 25% lotion diluted 1:3 (10 ml with 20 ml water) all over body, including scalp, face and ears, avoiding eyes and mouth.
Leave lotion 24 hours then wash off, repeat after 1 week.
Check and treat all household members, wash and sun-dry all bedding and clothes.
Do RDT for malaria. If positive, call AHC for malaria treatment.
Come back in 2 days, or sooner if baby gets worse, stops feeding, or has fever.

ACTION: ADVISE
STM: PERTUSSIS (WHOOPING COUGH)
---
Givim azithromycin 80 mg wan taem long dei fo 5 dei, no stop taem kofi i go daon.
Sapos bebi i stop brething, i go blu, o i go moa sik long kofi, kolem AHC long radio kwiktaem.
Lukluk gud fo saen blong denja: no fit dring, toraot evri samting, slip tumas, sek-sek.
Kambak long 2 dei sapos kofi i no go daon, o kwiktaem sapos hemi go blu o stop brething.

ACTION: ASK_PERSON

Ask the nurse in charge or the clinic supervisor what to do.
Also phone the AHC or NRH social worker or the police, and tell them: child 12 months, 8.9 kg, suspected abuse, mother says no, you want to keep the child.
Keep the child safe and do not leave alone while you wait for advice.

ACTION: REFER_NEXT_TRANSPORT
STM: NEWBORN BABIES - NEONATAL INFECTIONS
---
Poor feeding and fever in a 6 day old baby is a danger sign, so send her on the next boat.
Start ampicillin 145 mg (50 mg/kg) IV or IM and gentamicin 14.5 mg (5 mg/kg) IV or IM now.
Keep the baby warm, keep offering breast milk, and check her breathing often.
Call the AHC or hospital by radio or phone now to say she is coming.
Write the note: age, weight, feeding, temperature, drugs and times.

ACTION: REFER_NEXT_TRANSPORT
STM: MALARIA
---
Convulsion and drowsiness are danger signs. This child must go to hospital on the next boat.
While waiting, give artesunate 23 mg IM (10 mg/kg) if you have it, or artesunate 230 mg PR (10 mg/kg) if no injection.
If no artesunate, give any available ACT by mouth if the child can swallow, or refer for parenteral treatment.
Check blood sugar if you can. Keep the child on the side, clear airway, watch for more fits.
Call the AHC or hospital by radio now to say a severe malaria case is coming.
Write the referral note: age, weight, convulsion, drowsiness, jaundice, drugs and times.

No givim tin milk o susu kap yet, hem mas stap 12 mons fo stop susu.
Sapos bebi no gud gain weight, lukim sapos hem dring gud an solod gud.
Kambak long 1 wik sapos bebi no gud gain weight, o kwiktaem sapos hem no fit dring o hem toraot evri samting.

Sapos no IV, givim long maot sapos hem save hol, o no givim.
Kipim bebi warm, letem mama sidaon long hem.
Kolem hospital long radio nao, talem bebi hem kam.
Raetem referral leta: 2 mons, 4.3 kg, no fit dring, hot bodi, stif nek, meresin an taem.

ACTION: REFER_NOW
STM: NEWBORN BABIES - NEONATAL INFECTIONS
---
This is severe neonatal sepsis with danger signs: not passing urine, lethargy, fever, and infected umbilicus. Call AHC by HF radio immediately for emergency evacuation advice.
Start cefotaxime 180 mg (50 mg/kg) IV or IM now, then every 8 hours. If no cefotaxime, give ampicillin and gentamicin as per sepsis section.
Keep baby warm with skin-to-skin, express breast milk and put on nipple for sucking if any response.
Write referral note: age 5 days, weight 3.6 kg, home birth, no urine today, lethargic, fever, umbilical infection, cefotaxime dose and time.

Burns on the face and both hands are serious, so send him to hospital now in the truck.
Cover the burns with a clean dry cloth and do not put any ointment or oil on them.
Keep him warm and give fluids by mouth if he is awake and can swallow.
Call the hospital or AHC to say he is coming.
Write the note: age, weight, where the burns are, and the time.
